item.title: Offensive AI Con Unites Senior Researchers for AI-Powered Cyber Offense
item.description:
Offensive AI Con Unites Senior Researchers for AI-Powered Cyber Offense

Offensive AI Con (OAIC) is an invite‑only technical conference that examined the intersection of artificial intelligence and offensive cybersecurity. Held in Oceanside, San Diego, the event gathered senior security researchers, AI/ML engineers, and government defense representatives to discuss AI‑driven vulnerability discovery and exploit development.

🔍 Overview

  • Invite‑only, non‑commercial format prioritizing research collaboration over vendor presentations
  • Hosted in Oceanside, San Diego
  • Structured around technical talks, confidential breakout sessions, and networking receptions
  • Targets senior technical professionals working in offensive security and AI research

🎯 Topics Covered

  • AI‑based vulnerability research
  • Autonomous and semi‑autonomous offensive cyber operations
  • Methods for accelerating exploit development
  • Specialized datasets, model training strategies, scaffolding techniques, and binary analysis
  • OODA (observe, orient, decide, act) workflows and reducing cognitive strain for security operators
  • Multi‑agent strategies and AI‑based target identification

⚖️ Ethics & Policy

  • Responsible‑use frameworks for offensive AI capabilities
  • Discussion of unintended acceleration of cyber‑warfare capabilities
  • Strategic approaches to safeguarding organizations
  • Policy sessions with industry and government perspectives to examine how offensive AI research should be conducted and governed
  • Efforts to establish norms and coordination mechanisms as AI capabilities in offensive security advance

👥 Attendee Profile

  • Heads of security research, CTOs, research engineers, distinguished engineers, and technical staff from AI labs
  • Government and defense representatives from the Department of Defense and intelligence community organizations
  • Practitioners and policymakers interested in AI/ML applications in security contexts

🛡️ Sponsors

  • Microsoft Security
  • Google DeepMind
  • SpecterOps
  • SANS Institute
  • Cato Networks
  • Codewall.ai
  • Praetorian
  • Trail of Bits
  • Mindgard.ai
  • Zenity
  • Xbow
  • Bugcrowd
  • Cohere
  • Team Cymru
  • Dreadnode
  • RemoteThreat

item.title: US urges Europe to tap diesel reserves to lower fuel prices
item.description:
US urges Europe to tap diesel reserves to lower fuel prices

The United States is pressing European governments to release a portion of their strategic diesel reserves in order to ease price pressures and address supply disruptions.

🔍 Overview

  • The American Secretary of Energy, Chris Wright, proposed a coordinated plan to release diesel from European strategic reserves.
  • The proposal targets 120 million barrels of diesel over 180 days.
  • This amount is more than one‑third of the roughly 315 million barrels that EU countries held in reserve in June.
  • US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also supported the measure in a post on X.
  • President Donald Trump indicated he could ask Europe to tap their diesel reserves during a visit to Texas.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Release target: 120 million barrels of diesel.
  • Time frame: 180 days.
  • Share of EU reserves: > 33 % of the 315 million barrels reported in June.
  • Winter timing: The minister said, “It is time to bring the diesel stocks to market in a coordinated manner,” as winter approaches.

🗣️ Political Statements

  • Chris Wright told Fox News, “Europe can also contribute to improving the situation.”
  • Scott Bessent wrote on X, “Our European partners should accelerate the implementation of their existing commitments and make additional supplies immediately available to address ongoing disruptions.”
  • President Donald Trump said in Texas, “We could do that. They have diesel,” indicating he could ask Europe to release reserves.
  • On Thursday, Trump’s tone was described as less forceful.

💡 Why it matters

  • Releasing diesel could help lower fuel prices in the United States and Europe.
  • Coordinated market entry aims to stabilize supply ahead of the winter heating season.
  • The request reflects ongoing tensions over President Trump’s earlier threat to impose an export ban on US diesel.
  • European participation would demonstrate trans‑Atlantic cooperation on energy security.

#Diesel #EnergyPolicy #USEuropeRelations

Source: US government calls on Europe to release part of diesel reserves to lower prices

item.title: UNESCO and ENS Launch AI Ethics Call for Early‑Career Researchers
item.description:
UNESCO and ENS Launch AI Ethics Call for Early‑Career Researchers

UNESCO and the AI and Society Institute at École normale supérieure (ENS‑PSL) have opened a call for papers inviting researchers who earned their PhD within the last five years to submit proposals on the ethics of artificial intelligence.

🔍 Overview

  • The initiative follows UNESCO’s 2021 Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence.
  • It aims to promote emerging research, foster interdisciplinary exchange, and link scholarship with public policy and practice.

📅 Key Details

  • Selected proposals will be invited to present at a one‑day academic event in Paris on 10 December 2026.
  • The event will gather emerging scholars, established researchers, and institutional representatives for thematic discussions and expert feedback.
  • General participation is open to everyone; registration will be available on UNESCO’s website.

🎓 Eligibility

  • Researchers who completed a PhD within the past five years.
  • Work must address issues related to AI ethics.
  • Applications are welcomed from all disciplines and geographic regions.
  • Interdisciplinary, cross‑sectoral, theoretical, empirical, comparative, and practice‑oriented contributions are encouraged.
  • Co‑authored proposals are allowed if all authors meet the eligibility criteria.

📝 Submission Guidelines

  • Submit an extended abstract of 800–1,000 words (references excluded) in English, in Word or PDF format.
  • Abstracts must be anonymized (no author names or identifying information).
  • Proposals will be reviewed by laureates and jury members of the UNESCO Beruniy Prize for Scientific Research on the Ethics of AI.
  • Successful applicants will be notified by 15 November 2026 and asked to deliver a full paper of 5,000–7,000 words by 1 December 2026.

✈️ Travel Support

  • One selected author will receive travel support to attend the Paris event, alongside members of the UNESCO Beruniy Prize International Jury and Laureates.

📚 Post‑Event Opportunities

  • Proceedings will be compiled by UNESCO and the AI and Society Institute.
  • Selected authors may adapt their research for publication in the Tribune of the Conseil de l’intelligence artificielle et du numérique (CIANum), reaching a broader public and policy audience.

#UNESCO #AIethics #CallForPapers #Research

Source: Call for papers: Advancing research on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

item.title: Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act Introduced in Congress
item.description:
Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act Introduced in Congress

Senator Bernie Sanders (I‑VT) and Representative Greg Casar (D‑TX) have introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, which would prohibit the development of artificial superintelligence and pause advanced AI systems.

🔍 Overview

  • The bill defines artificial superintelligence as technology capable of the “destruction or disempowerment of humanity,” including overthrowing the government.
  • It also pauses development of “frontier models,” which lawmakers classify as advanced AI systems trained on a specific data threshold.

⚙️ How the Bill Works

  • A scientist‑led Department of Artificial Intelligence would be created to oversee the technology.
  • AI companies must obtain permission from this department before developing advanced AI models.
  • The department would monitor frontier AI models, remove dangerous features, and supervise the destruction of artificial superintelligence.
  • Development of advanced AI could resume only after the department is established.

⚖️ Penalties

  • AI leaders who violate the law could face up to 20 years in prison.
  • The same penalty applies to “rogue actors” who break the rules but are not employed by an AI company.
  • The penalty is described as “similar to existing penalties related to unlawfully developing nuclear weapons.”

📊 Context

  • A former Anthropic researcher warned there is more than a 10 percent chance AI could “kill all humans” by the end of the decade.
  • Last week, California Governor Gavin Newsom proposed a “kill switch” for frontier models.

#AIRegulation #ArtificialSuperintelligence #USLegislation

Source: Bernie Sanders proposes banning ‘superintelligence’ and putting violators in prison
